The chance that a vowel is one of a pair is the sum of their percentages. Pair sums: AE 65, AI 35, AO 28, AU 32, EI 60, EO 53, EU 57, IO 23, IU 27, OU 20. Those above 34% are AE, AI, EI, EO and EU, which is 5 pairs.
The three least frequent vowels are O (8), U (12) and I (15), totalling 35. The most frequent of them is I, and 15/35 = 3/7 = 42 6/7 %.
O and U together are 8 + 12 = 20% of vowels, so the total is 5040 / 0.20 = 25200. E is 45% of this: 0.45 x 25200 = 11340.

If the number is 100a + 10b + c, the difference from its reverse is 99(a - c) = 396, so a - c = 4. With the reversed number also a three-digit number (c not 0) there are 5 pairs (a, c) = (5,1) to (9,5), and the middle digit can be any of the 8 digits other than a and c, giving 5 x 8 = 40. Allowing c = 0 would give 48, which is not offered, so the intended reading is 40.
